# Repository Surface Catalog (API, Examples, and Managed Documents)

**Status:** Active  
**Spec / Decision ID:** `CA-SURFACE-CATALOG-001`  
**Owner:** Framework Architecture & Documentation Governance  
**Canonical JSON Catalogs:**
- [`catalog/repository-surface/api-surface.v1.json`](../../../catalog/repository-surface/api-surface.v1.json)
- [`catalog/repository-surface/example-surface.v1.json`](../../../catalog/repository-surface/example-surface.v1.json)
- [`catalog/repository-surface/document-surface.v1.json`](../../../catalog/repository-surface/document-surface.v1.json)

This specification defines the principles, schema standards, and complete inventory for three repository surfaces:

1. **Full Repository API Architecture**: all 18 workspace packages (`packages/*`), their public `exports`, workspace dependencies, and stability tiers.
2. **What Examples Explain**: all 77 canonical routes across 13 semantic groups in `example/`, standalone demos (`demos/bolt-style-editor`, `examples/vanilla-js`), 5 package-local example suites, and 9 narrative example walkthroughs.
3. **Managed Documentation Architecture**: all 9 root markdown documents, 12 managed documentation areas with explicit authority and EN/KO pairing policies, and derived LLMS bundle artifacts.

It complements [Package Boundary and Codebase Management](/en/context-layered/package-boundary-convention), [Specification, Issue, and Documentation Management](/en/context-layered/change-management-convention), [Documentation and Development Management](/en/concept/documentation-development-conventions), and ADR [CA-SURFACE-CATALOG-001](/en/context-layered/decisions/CA-SURFACE-CATALOG-001).

---

## 1. Five Organizing Principles

1. **Source-First Non-Duplication**: Runtime manifests (`packages/*/package.json`), route registration (`example/src/App.tsx`), package READMEs/contracts, and handwritten guides (`docs/{en,ko}/**`) remain the canonical sources of truth. The surface catalog indexes and cross-validates them without duplicating behavior specs.
2. **Explicit Authority vs. Derived Separation**: Every managed document is classified as `authoritative`, `discovery`, `evidence`, `derived`, `transitional`, or `historical`. Derived files (`docs/{en,ko}/llms/llms-*.txt`) must be regenerated from source, never edited as canonical specs.
3. **Three-Surface Versioned Schema Symmetry**: API (`api-surface.v1.json`), Example (`example-surface.v1.json`), and Document (`document-surface.v1.json`) share versioned schemas, stable kebab IDs, bilingual summaries (`en` / `ko`), and explicit verification gates.
4. **Honest Bilingual Parity Accounting**: Directories expected to move in lockstep use `strict-paired` (0 unpaired files; currently all 5 `docs/{en,ko}/{context-layered,concept,examples,guide,troubleshooting}` and `docs/{en,ko}/llms`). Any directory temporarily carrying tracked translation debt uses `tracked-partial` with an explicit `knownUnpaired` list so gaps cannot silently grow or go stale.
5. **Fail-Closed Drift Verification**: Any uncataloged package, export subpath, workspace dependency, canonical example route, package example folder, root markdown file, or translation drift fails `pnpm verify:surface-catalog` and `pnpm convention:check`.

---

## 2. Base Specification

### Package Layers & Stability Tiers (`api-surface.v1.json`)

| Layer | Role | Stability Tiers Used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `foundation` | Zero/minimal-dependency core contracts & engines (`core`, `store-core`, `mutative-core`, `tool-protocol`, `tool-durable-operations`) | `stable`, `public-preview` |
| `framework-adapter` | Framework-specific bindings (`react`, `mutative`, `lit`, `preact`) | `stable`, `public-preview` |
| `ui-runtime` | Owned DOM roots, Web Components, FACE, SSR/hydration (`lit-ui`, `preact-ui`) | `public-preview` |
| `integration-adapter` | External protocol & runtime bridges (`ai-sdk`, `webmcp`, `xstate`) | `public-preview` |
| `tooling` | Build/doc/style verification tooling (`style-testing`) | `private` |
| `private-host-support` | Private demo/template support (`live-code-editor`, `openrouter-browser-storage`, `template-react`) | `private` |

### Document Authority Classes & Pairing Policies (`document-surface.v1.json`)

| Authority Class | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `authoritative` | Canonical specification, architecture convention, or user guide |
| `discovery` | Landing README, AI agent guide, or index linking to canonical docs |
| `evidence` | Immutable release plans, v1 audit/runbook records, verification evidence |
| `derived` | Machine-generated outputs (`docs/{en,ko}/llms/llms-*.txt` via `pnpm docs:llms`) |
| `transitional` | Retained bridge documentation pending consolidation |
| `historical` | Preserved point-in-time snapshot (`CHANGELOG.md`) |

| Pairing Policy | Enforcement Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `strict-paired` | `enDir` and `koDir` must match 1:1 on `.md` files (0 EN-only, 0 KO-only) |
| `tracked-partial` | `onlyEn` and `onlyKo` sets must match `knownUnpaired` 1:1 until translated |
| `single-locale` | Single authoritative locale (`releases/`, `docs/releases/`, `packages/*/docs/`) |
| `derived` | Generated artifact bound to a documented `sourceOfTruth` and generator command |
| `not-applicable` | Machine schemas/skills (`catalog/`, `skills/`, `.agents/skills/`) |

### Update Loop on Surface Changes

1. Update the canonical source (`package.json`, `example/src/App.tsx`, or `docs/`).
2. Update the corresponding catalog in `catalog/repository-surface/*.v1.json` and, if needed, `docs/{en,ko}/context-layered/repository-surface-catalog.md`.
3. Run `pnpm docs:llms` for edited markdown files to regenerate `docs/{en,ko}/llms/llms-*.txt`.
4. Run `pnpm verify:surface-catalog && pnpm convention:check && pnpm docs:check`.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **API Surface Source of Truth**: Rather than maintaining a repository-wide TypeDoc HTML/Markdown generation tree (`docs/en/api/**`), all 14 public runtime packages document their public contracts directly in `packages/*/README.md`, `packages/*/docs/*.md`, TypeScript `.d.ts` declarations, and [`catalog/repository-surface/api-surface.v1.json`](../../../catalog/repository-surface/api-surface.v1.json).

### 3.1 Package Roles by Layer

- **Foundation (`5`)**: `core` (action pipeline & optional `./element` DOM/host transport), `store-core` (framework-neutral state/timeline/transaction protocols + `createStateStore`), `mutative-core` (`mutative@2.0.2`-compatible immutable draft/patch engine), `tool-protocol` (Zod/JSON Schema tools, MCP/provider adapters, approval queues, idempotency, observability), `tool-durable-operations` (lease/claim side-effect recovery & IndexedDB/Redis/PostgreSQL reference backends).
- **Framework Adapters (`4`)**: `react` (React 18/19 Action/Store/TimeTravel/Ref contexts, hooks, transactions, `./refs`, `./time-travel`, `./transactions`, `./backend`, `./advanced`, `./webmcp`), `mutative` (`TimeTravel` + `MutativeStateBackend`/`MutativeTimelineBackend`), `lit` (`StoreController`, `ActionController`, `ControllerScope`), `preact` (`createDispatchContext`, `connectSourceSignal`, `createSourceContext`, `useProjection`).
- **UI Runtimes (`2`)**: `lit-ui` (Lit Web Components, W3C Context Protocol, FACE, `./react-bridge`, `./ssr`, `./hydrate`), `preact-ui` (owned Preact DOM roots, `mountPreact`/`hydratePreact`, `createDisposalScope`, `./react-bridge`, `./ssr`).
- **Integration Adapters (`3`)**: `xstate` (XState v5/v6 actor bridges in `.` and Effect v4 / `@xstate/effect` / Standard Schema v1 / transaction scopes in `./effect`), `ai-sdk` (AI SDK v7 turn-scoped `ToolSet` bridge), `webmcp` (allowlisted `document.modelContext` browser adapter).
- **Tooling (`1`)**: `style-testing` (private Playwright style extraction & Babel instrumentation).
- **Private Host Support (`3`)**: `live-code-editor` (workspace snapshot & iframe preview bridge), `openrouter-browser-storage` (demo API key local storage), `template-react` (Context-Layered + Astryx starter template).

For deciding which state/store API to use across these packages, see the [Store Selection and Usage Guide](./store-selection-and-usage-guide.md).

# Spec-to-Code Authoring Guide

**Status:** Active  
**Spec / Decision IDs:** `CA-SURFACE-CATALOG-001`, `CA-SPEC-EVIDENCE-001`, `CA-STATECHART-EFFECT-001`, `CA-ELEMENT-INTEROP-001`  
**Owner:** Framework Core, React Runtime & Architecture Governance  
**Related Specifications:**
- [Convention Index](./convention-index.md)
- [Implementation Convention](./implementation-convention.md)
- [Store Selection and Usage Guide](./store-selection-and-usage-guide.md)
- [Core Action Contracts](../../../packages/core/docs/action-contracts.md)
- [React State Contracts](../../../packages/react/docs/state-contracts.md)
- [Interaction Intent to Implementation Flow](./interaction-intent-implementation-flow.md)
- [Unified Triad Self-Serve Sync Guide](./triad-evidence-sync-guide.md)

Context-Action is designed so that **specification intent, domain state, execution pipelines, UI bindings, and verification gates map 1:1 to distinct code locations**. Rather than jumping between seven separate manuals before writing a feature, use this guide as the single end-to-end blueprint connecting specs to idiomatic Context-Action code.

## 1. End-to-End Spec-to-Code Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S0["Stage 0: Design and State Classification - IIC (CA-IIC-*) + 3-Tier State Rule (CA-SPEC-EVIDENCE-001)"]
    S1["Stage 1: Boundaries and Ownership - contexts/ (Business vs Layout Intent) + Store Selection"]
    S2["Stage 2: Pure Domain Rules - business/ (Zero Framework Imports + @evidenceReview Policy Hopping)"]
    S3["Stage 3: Execution Orchestration - runtime/ (Headless Core) or handlers/ (React Registry) + 4-Role Pipeline"]
    S4["Stage 4: Thin UI and Host Surface - actions/ + hooks/ + views/ (@evidenceExclude, 6-Level Layout, Multi-Host Readers)"]
    S5["Stage 5: Automated Evidence and Gates - convention:check, package-boundary:check, verify:surface-catalog, docs:check, verify:quick"]

    S0 --> S1
    S1 --> S2
    S2 --> S3
    S3 --> S4
    S4 --> S5
    S5 -. "Reverse Forensics on Failures" .-> S0
```

## 2. Spec-to-Layer-to-Gate Mapping Matrix

| Authoring Stage | Target Directory / Artifact | Core Coding Rule | Authoritative Spec | Enforcement Scope & Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Stage 0 · Intent & Tiering** | Design spec / PR / `@evidence*` | Record UX shortcuts & fallback signals (`CA-IIC-*`); apply **2-Second State Rule** (`Tier 1` TypeSpec + `@evidenceReview`, `Tier 2` client rules/activity, `Tier 3` volatile UI waived) | [IIC Flow](./interaction-intent-implementation-flow.md), [CA-SPEC-EVIDENCE-001](./decisions/CA-SPEC-EVIDENCE-001.md) | **Advisory / Cross-Repo** (fail-closed when running sibling `ttsc-ex` / `oa-sdk` Policy Hopping checks) |
| **Stage 1 · Boundaries & Store Selection** | `contexts/` (`*Contexts.tsx`, `*Context.ts`) | Separate **`BusinessActionIntent`** from **`LayoutActionIntent`** (**No Mixed Payloads**); choose progressive adoption level (`Level 1 Lite`, `Level 2 Standard Headless-First DI`, `Level 3 Enterprise 6-Layer`); pick primitive from Store matrix | [Store Selection Guide](./store-selection-and-usage-guide.md), [Triad Sync Guide](./triad-evidence-sync-guide.md) | **CI-Enforced**: `pnpm convention:check`, `pnpm package-boundary:check` |
| **Stage 2 · Pure Domain Logic** | `business/` (`*Draft.ts`, `*Validation.ts`, `*Result.ts`, `*Activity.ts`, `*StateMachine.ts`) | **Zero React & `@context-action/*` imports**; pure `state + event -> nextState` transitions; no UI copy or DOM calls; emit structured domain events instead of UI strings | [Implementation Convention](./implementation-convention.md), [Explicit State Machine](./patterns/explicit-state-machine.md) | **CI-Enforced**: `pnpm convention:check` (`business/` filename + import boundary rules) |
| **Stage 3A · Headless Engine (Optional)** | `runtime/` (`create*.ts`, `*.test.ts`) | Pure TypeScript engine assembly (`ActionRegister` + `createStore` / `createStateStore` / `TimeTravelStoreManager`) runnable in Node/Workers/Preact/Lit; **zero `react`/`react-dom` or React layer imports**; test directly without DOM | [Context-Layered Guide](./context-layered-guide.md), [Headless-First Showcase](/en/examples/basic-setup) | **CI-Enforced**: `pnpm convention:check` (`runtime/` `.ts` naming + zero React/UI imports) |
| **Stage 3B · React Orchestration** | `handlers/` (`*HandlerRegistry.tsx`, `use*Handlers.tsx`, `*HandlerSupport.ts`) | Three-step commit loop (`getValue()` -> `business/` -> `setValue()`/`update()`); use **4-role hooks**; coordinate multi-store atomic undo via `StoreTransactionCoordinator` / `bindActionTransactions`; hydrate decoupled `@entityRoot` + `@aspectOf` storage via `Promise.allSettled` | [Core Action Contracts](../../../packages/core/docs/action-contracts.md), [React State Contracts](../../../packages/react/docs/state-contracts.md) | **CI-Enforced**: `pnpm convention:check` (forbids direct `use*ActionGuard`/`CommandHandler`/`Observer`/`ResultHandler`/`ActionHandler` outside `handlers/` and enforces `Action -> Store -> Ref -> Registry` nesting) |
| **Stage 4 · Thin Surface & Host Bridges** | `actions/`, `hooks/`, `views/` (`.tsx`) | `actions/` exposes semantic commands (hides raw `dispatch`); `hooks/` computes derived view models via `StoreReader`; `views/` has top-of-file `@evidenceExclude`, zero `runtime/`/`business/`/`handlers/` runtime imports, 6-Level layout hierarchy, 4-Tier semantic Z-Index (`--z-base`..`--z-toast`); bridge Preact/Lit read-only | [Folder Structure](./architecture/folder-structure.md), [CA-ELEMENT-INTEROP-001](./decisions/CA-ELEMENT-INTEROP-001.md) | **CI-Enforced**: `pnpm convention:check`, `pnpm --filter example check`, `pnpm verify:element-interop` |
| **Stage 5 · Catalog, Docs & Receipt** | `catalog/repository-surface/*.json`, paired `docs/{en,ko}/**`, `.verification/local-receipt.json` | Update paired EN/KO docs, `api/example/document-surface.v1.json`, `docs/{en,ko}/llms/llms-*.txt` (`pnpm docs:llms`), and compile-checked `<!-- @context-action-compile -->` blocks; mint local receipt on clean commit | [Documentation Conventions](../concept/documentation-development-conventions.md), [CA-SURFACE-CATALOG-001](./decisions/CA-SURFACE-CATALOG-001.md) | **CI-Enforced**: `pnpm verify:surface-catalog`, `pnpm verify:doc-snippets`, `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm verify:quick`, `pnpm verify:receipt` |

## 3. Recommended 4-Role Action API Hierarchy

Context-Action distinguishes four explicit execution roles inside an Action Pipeline (`Admission -> Execution & Result -> Settlement`). Prefer the dedicated role APIs for structured workflows so admission checks, state commits, return values, and post-settlement telemetry cannot accidentally mix responsibilities:

| Tier | Core `ActionRegister` API | React `ActionContext` Hook | Intended Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Canonical · Guard (Admission)** | `registerGuard(action, fn, config)` | `useActionGuard` | Validate payloads/permissions before mutation; short-circuit via `controller.abort()`. |
| **Canonical · Command (Execution)** | `registerCommand(action, fn, config)` | `useActionCommandHandler` | Execute domain work and commit stores (`getValue()` -> `business/` -> `setValue()`/`update()`). |
| **Canonical · Result (Value Return)** | `registerResult(action, fn, config)` | `useActionResultHandler` | Compute typed return values collected by `dispatchWithResult()`. |
| **Canonical · Observer (Observation)** | `registerObserver(action, fn, config)` | `useActionObserver` | Observe settled outcomes (`event.result`, `event.outcome`) for logs/telemetry/UI sync with zero abort or return authority. |
| **Lite / Compatibility** | `register(action, fn, config)` | `useActionHandler` | General-purpose hook allowed for Level 1 Lite features or legacy migration. |
| **Deprecated Transitional** | `registerEffect(action, fn, config)` | `useActionEffectHandler` | **Deprecated.** Migrate `effectKind: 'guard'` to `useActionGuard` and `effectKind: 'observer'` to `useActionObserver`. |

---

## 4. End-to-End Authoring Walkthrough (Spec -> Headless Runtime -> React DI)

The following compile-checked snippet demonstrates the recommended **Headless-First Symmetric DI** pattern combining separated intents (`BusinessActionIntent` vs `LayoutActionIntent`), pure `business/` validation/calculation, a zero-React `createStateStore` + `ActionRegister` 4-role pipeline, and `ownership="shared"` React Context injection:

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```tsx
import { ActionRegister, type ActionPayloadMap } from '@context-action/core';
import { createStateStore, type StateMutationMeta } from '@context-action/store-core';
import {
  createActionContext,
  createStore,
  createStoreContext,
  useStoreValue,
} from '@context-action/react';
import { createBackendStore } from '@context-action/react/backend';

// Stage 1: Separate BusinessActionIntent from LayoutActionIntent (No Mixed Payloads)
interface OrderBusinessActions extends ActionPayloadMap {
  submitOrder: { sku: string; qty: number };
}

interface OrderResultMap {
  submitOrder: { accepted: boolean; total: number };
}

interface OrderLayoutActions extends ActionPayloadMap {
  toggleSummaryDrawer: { open?: boolean };
}

interface OrderState {
  readonly lastSku: string | null;
  readonly total: number;
  readonly error: string | null;
}

// Stage 2: Pure business/ rules (zero framework imports)
function validateOrderInput(sku: string, qty: number): string | null {
  if (!sku.trim()) return 'SKU is required.';
  if (qty <= 0) return 'Quantity must be positive.';
  return null;
}

function computeOrderTotal(qty: number): number {
  return qty * 25;
}

// Stage 3A: Pure-TS Headless runtime/ assembly (runnable in Node, Workers, Preact, Lit, React)
export function createHeadlessOrderRuntime() {
  const initialOrder: OrderState = { lastSku: null, total: 0, error: null };
  const orderStore = createStore<OrderState>('order', initialOrder);
  const telemetryBackend = createStateStore('telemetry', { completedCount: 0 });
  const telemetryReactStore = createBackendStore('telemetry', telemetryBackend, {
    ownership: 'shared',
  });

  const register = new ActionRegister<OrderBusinessActions, OrderResultMap>({
    name: 'OrderEngine',
  });

  // Guard (Admission): validate before state mutation
  register.registerGuard(
    'submitOrder',
    ({ sku, qty }, controller) => {
      const error = validateOrderInput(sku, qty);
      if (error) {
        orderStore.update((prev) => ({ ...prev, error }));
        controller.abort(error);
      }
    },
    { id: 'order-input-guard', priority: 100 },
  );

  // Command / Result: compute pure logic and commit state
  register.registerResult(
    'submitOrder',
    ({ sku, qty }) => {
      const total = computeOrderTotal(qty);
      orderStore.setValue({ lastSku: sku.trim(), total, error: null });
      return { accepted: true, total };
    },
    { id: 'order-submit-command', priority: 10 },
  );

  // Observer: react after pipeline settlement without controller or return authority
  register.registerObserver(
    'submitOrder',
    (event) => {
      if (event.outcome === 'completed') {
        const meta: StateMutationMeta = { origin: 'system', label: 'order-settled' };
        telemetryBackend.update((prev) => ({ completedCount: prev.completedCount + 1 }), meta);
      }
    },
    { id: 'order-audit-observer', priority: 1 },
  );

  const LayoutActions = createActionContext<OrderLayoutActions>('OrderLayout');
  const BusinessActions = createActionContext<OrderBusinessActions, OrderResultMap>('OrderBusiness');
  const OrderStores = createStoreContext('OrderStores', {
    order: { initialValue: initialOrder },
    // Tier 3 volatile presentation state waived from TypeSpec
    drawerOpen: false,
  });

  return {
    orderStore,
    telemetryReactStore,
    register,
    BusinessActions,
    LayoutActions,
    OrderStores,
  };
}

const runtime = createHeadlessOrderRuntime();

// Stage 4: Thin React View with Symmetric DI (ownership="shared")
function OrderPanel() {
  const dispatch = runtime.BusinessActions.useActionDispatch();
  const orderStore = runtime.OrderStores.useStore('order');
  const order = useStoreValue(orderStore);
  const telemetry = useStoreValue(runtime.telemetryReactStore);

  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={() => void dispatch('submitOrder', { sku: 'CA-BOOK', qty: 2 })}
    >
      Last Total: {order.total} (Completed: {telemetry.completedCount})
    </button>
  );
}

export function OrderFeature() {
  return (
    <runtime.BusinessActions.Provider register={runtime.register} ownership="shared">
      <runtime.OrderStores.Provider
        stores={{ order: runtime.orderStore }}
        ownership="shared"
      >
        <OrderPanel />
      </runtime.OrderStores.Provider>
    </runtime.BusinessActions.Provider>
  );
}
```

> **Progressive Adoption Rule:** Small local UI features can start at **Level 1 Lite** with `createActionContext` + `createStoreContext` + `useActionHandler`. Move domain rules into `business/` and headless `runtime/` as soon as validation/state transitions should be tested outside React or shared across host frameworks.

---

## 5. Multi-Host Store Reader Bridges (`React` · `Preact` · `Lit`)

When sharing one headless `StateStore` (`@context-action/store-core`) or `@context-action/react` `Store` across multiple UI runtimes, note the exact structural `getSnapshot()` shape expected by each host adapter:

| Host Adapter | Reader Contract | `getSnapshot()` Return Shape | Explicit Bridge Needed? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **React** (`@context-action/react`, `@context-action/react/backend`) | `StoreReader<T>` / `StateReader<T>` | `Snapshot<T>` (`{ value, name, lastUpdate, version? }`) | No for `Store` / `TimeTravelStore`; wrap custom `StateBackend` with `createBackendStore()` |
| **Preact Signals** (`@context-action/preact`) | `ReadableSource<T>` | **Raw value `T`** | Use **`fromStateReader(reader)`** to unwrap `{ value: T }` cleanly into `ReadableSource<T>` |
| **Lit** (`@context-action/lit`) | `ReadableStore<T>` | `getValue(): T` (+ `subscribe`) | No for `Store`, `TimeTravelStore`, or `createStateStore()` |

Because a domain state `T` might itself contain a `.value` property, `@context-action/preact` intentionally avoids ambiguous `'value' in snapshot` duck-typing inside `connectSourceSignal()` and provides an explicit `fromStateReader()` adapter instead:

```ts
import { createStateStore } from '@context-action/store-core';
import { connectSourceSignal, fromStateReader } from '@context-action/preact';
import { StoreController } from '@context-action/lit';

// One framework-neutral store owned outside UI runtimes
export const sharedSessionStore = createStateStore('session', { step: 1 });

// 1. Preact Signals read-only projection (explicit unwrapping via fromStateReader)
export const preactSession = connectSourceSignal(fromStateReader(sharedSessionStore));

// 2. Lit ReactiveController projection (directly accepts StateStore because it implements getValue + subscribe)
// Inside a LitElement host:
// private session = new StoreController(this, sharedSessionStore);
```

---

## 6. Progressive Adoption, Defect Prevention & Debt Governance

Avoid over-engineering simple UI widgets while guaranteeing strict invariants once workflows scale.

### 6.1 3-Level Progressive Adoption Matrix

| Adoption Level | Minimal Directory Shape | Required Primitives | Promote Next When… |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Level 1 · Lite** | `contexts/`, `handlers/`, `views/` | `createActionContext` + `createStoreContext` + `useActionHandler` | Business validation or async transitions need unit testing outside React |
| **Level 2 · Headless-First Symmetric DI** | Add `business/`, pure-TS `runtime/` | `ActionRegister` + `createStateStore`/`createStore` + `ownership="shared"` Providers | Multiple UI views/runtimes (`React`, `Preact`, `Lit`, Workers) share the same engine |
| **Level 3 · Full 6-Layer** | Full `contexts / business / runtime (opt.) / handlers / actions / hooks / views` | Separated `Business` vs. `Layout` ActionContexts, `RefContext`, 4-role hooks, structured FSM/events | Teams enforce long-lived domain contracts, IIC traceability, and TypeSpec Evidence (`packages/template-react` starter) |

### 6.2 What Each Pattern Induces (Intent & Quality Guarantees)

- **Handler-only lazy reads (`no-store-subscription-in-handlers`) + `useCallback`**: Prevents stale-closure reads, unintended handler unregistration/re-registration churn, and circular re-render loops.
- **Dispatch-only `actions/` helpers (`no-store-access-in-actions`)**: Keeps components unable to bypass Guards or Observers with ad-hoc `store.setValue()` mutations.
- **Separated `BusinessActionIntent` vs. `LayoutActionIntent`**: Stops ephemeral layout events (`drawerToggle`, `focusField`) from triggering business analytics, persistence, or TimeTravel undo entries.
- **Structured domain codes & events in `business/` → UI text mapping in `hooks/`**: Ensures domain tests and analytics remain immune to UX wording changes and keeps localization in the binding layer.
- **Explicit Debt Ledgers (`layered-surface-classification.json` & `rule-exceptions.json`)**: Every allowed deviation must declare a non-empty rationale and fails closed once stale, stopping architectural rot before it spreads.

---

===================[ DOC: en/context-layered/stability-test-cycle.md ]===================
# Stability Test Cycle for Context-Layered Architecture

This guide describes a test cycle designed to turn an intentionally layered architecture into a visible product advantage. The goal is not only to prove correctness, but to show that extra structure results in predictable behavior under change, stress, and maintenance.

## Why This Matters

Context-Layered Architecture can feel heavier than a minimal React setup. The payoff should therefore be demonstrated, not merely claimed.

The recommended message is:

- The architecture is more structured than a simple component-local approach.
- That extra structure creates strong runtime boundaries.
- Those boundaries are continuously verified by a layered test cycle.

## Supported Runtime Matrix

The published React package declares `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0` as its peer runtime.
CI verifies React 18.3.1 plus the minimum and current React 19.2 versions on
Node 24, which matches the repository engine requirement (`node >=24.11.0`).
React 19-only features such as `<Activity>` are covered by the React 19 lanes;
the common Store/Action/Context/Ref contract is checked on both major lines.
Node 22 is intentionally outside the support contract until the engine
requirement is lowered and the package matrix is updated together.

The compatibility job rebuilds Core and React, then runs React type-checks and
the packed consumer contract against React 18.3.1 and both supported 19.2
versions. Package export checks also cover both ESM and CommonJS entry points.

## The Stability-Oriented Test Cycle

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Contract Tests"] --> B["Implementation Pattern Tests"]
    B --> C["Real Interaction Scenario Tests"]
    C --> D["Stress and Regression Tests"]
    D --> E["Documentation Verification"]
```

If you want to evaluate whether the architecture earns its complexity, read this guide together with:

- [Canonical Order Form Example](/en/examples/canonical-order-form)
- [Context-Layered Architecture Guide](/en/context-layered/context-layered-guide)

### 1. Contract Tests

Contract tests protect the guarantees of each core factory and boundary.

- `createActionContext(contextName, config?)` must provide stable dispatch and safe handler registration.
- `createStoreContext(contextName, initialStores)` must create isolated typed stores with predictable subscriptions.
- `createRefContext()` must manage mount state, imperative access, and cleanup safely.

These tests answer the question: "What does the architecture promise?"

### 2. Implementation Pattern Tests

Implementation pattern tests verify the recommended architecture itself.

- `views` dispatch actions instead of embedding business logic.
- `handlers` orchestrate state changes and side effects.
- `business` remains pure and deterministic.
- `hooks` subscribe and derive view-friendly values.
- `refs` remain dedicated to imperative targets.

These tests answer the question: "Does the code follow the intended design?"

### 3. Real Interaction Scenario Tests

Scenario tests should behave like product stories, not utility checks.

- invalid form submission should surface field errors
- the first invalid field should receive focus through `RefContext`
- valid submission should pass through action, handler, business, and store layers
- reactive UI should update from store subscriptions instead of ad hoc local state

These tests answer the question: "Does the architecture hold during real user flows?"

### 4. Stress and Regression Tests

This layer is where the architecture proves its value.

- high-frequency updates
- repeated handler execution
- cleanup after rapid mount/unmount cycles
- cross-context isolation
- memory leak prevention
- patch-based subscription efficiency

These tests answer the question: "Does the design remain stable under pressure?"

### 5. Documentation Verification

Documentation must stay executable in spirit.

- example code in docs should match the current API
- canonical example structure should map to real files
- migration guides should reflect current implementation patterns

These checks answer the question: "Can users trust the architecture story?"

## CI Recommendation

Use multiple lanes instead of one monolithic pipeline.

### Fast PR Lane

- contract tests
- critical pattern tests
- type checks

### Extended PR Lane

- integration scenarios
- migration workflows
- canonical example flow tests

### Nightly Lane

- high-frequency performance suites
- cleanup and lifecycle stress tests
- long-running regression scenarios

### Release Lane

- full React package test suite
- example app type check and build
- documentation build and link validation

## Current Release Policy and Gate

Workspace packages follow independent semantic versioning rather than a single pre-1.0 lockstep line (for example Core `1.3.x`, Store Core `0.1.x`, Mutative Core `0.8.x`, Mutative `0.8.x`, React `4.0.x`, XState `0.1.x`, Lit `0.1.x`, Preact `0.1.x`/`0.2.x`; see [Repository Surface Catalog](/en/context-layered/repository-surface-catalog) and [`releases/RELEASE.md`](../../../releases/RELEASE.md)). An API move or removal is allowed only when its package changelog marks it as breaking, migration documentation names the replacement import, and the release gate tests the resulting packed artifact.

For React 4, the published `@context-action/react` entry exposes root stores/actions/refs plus `./backend`, `./advanced`, `./utils`, and `./webmcp`. The default `@context-action/react` entry remains free of Durable/tool protocol runtime dependencies, while `@context-action/react/tools` stays workspace-only for standalone development demos while Durable 0.2 is withheld.

For local pre-PR and local-first receipt verification ([Local-First Verification Policy](../../LOCAL_FIRST_VERIFICATION_POLICY.md)), run:

```bash
pnpm verify:quick   # Fast smoke gate (~15-35s) + .verification/local-receipt.json
pnpm verify         # Full 17-step local suite + .verification/local-receipt.json
pnpm verify:receipt # Audit cryptographic receipt integrity
```

Before a release candidate tag or protected workflow dispatch, run:

```bash
pnpm release:check
```

It runs the full local verification set, regenerates API docs, verifies that generated docs match, checks surface catalogs, and validates packed consumers and examples. Protected release workflows verify immutable commits and run post-publication consumer checks against:

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm type-check`
- `pnpm verify:package-exports` and `pnpm verify:package-tarballs`
- `pnpm verify:surface-catalog`, `pnpm convention:check`, and `pnpm package-boundary:check`
- `pnpm docs:check` (including `pnpm docs:management` and `pnpm llms:check`)
- a clean package version/changelog set and published-consumer smoke tests across the public package cohorts

## Recommended Assertions

Prefer assertions that reinforce architectural trust.

- handler side effects occur in the expected layer
- store updates are observable through subscriptions
- ref-driven focus or scroll behavior occurs without hidden local state
- business logic produces deterministic output from explicit inputs
- resetting a flow restores all participating stores to a known baseline

## Canonical Example Strategy

Each major architectural guide should have one canonical example that is:

- small enough to read in a single sitting
- realistic enough to resemble product code
- structured with `contexts`, `business`, `handlers`, `actions`, `hooks`, and `views`
- covered by tests that validate the actual example component

For this repository, the recommended canonical example is an implementation-first order form:

- draft state in stores
- validation as pure business logic
- submission orchestration in handlers
- field focus through refs
- subscription-based summary panels in hooks and views

## Success Criteria

The architecture is being communicated well when a new contributor can:

1. open one canonical example
2. trace the data flow from view to action to handler to store to view
3. run one focused test file
4. understand why the extra layers improve reliability

That is the point where "over-engineered" starts reading as "operationally stable."

===================[ DOC: en/context-layered/store-selection-and-usage-guide.md ]===================
# Store Selection and Usage Guide

**Status:** Active  
**Spec / Decision ID:** `CA-SURFACE-CATALOG-001`  
**Owner:** Framework Core & React Runtime  
**Related Specifications:**
- [Store and Time-Travel Contracts](../../../packages/react/docs/state-contracts.md)
- [Store Conventions](/en/concept/store-conventions)
- [Repository Surface Catalog](/en/context-layered/repository-surface-catalog)
- [Spec-to-Code Authoring Guide](/en/context-layered/spec-to-code-authoring-guide)
- [CA-STATECHART-EFFECT-001](/en/context-layered/decisions/CA-STATECHART-EFFECT-001)

Context-Action separates **write ownership** (`StoreWriter` / Action Handlers) from **read ownership** (`StoreReader` / reactive hooks or framework controllers). Every state mutation belongs inside an Action Handler following the three-step flow: read via `store.getValue()`, compute pure domain logic, and commit via `store.setValue()` or `store.update()`.

---

## 1. Store Selection Matrix

| Store / State Mechanism | Package Entry | Primary Use Case | Undo/Redo | React Dependency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **`createStoreContext`** | `@context-action/react` | **Default choice.** Scope multiple domain stores cleanly to a React component subtree | No | Yes |
| **`createStore` (`Store`)** | `@context-action/react` | Standalone module-level store, dependency-injected store, or unit tests | No | Yes (Mutative built in) |
| **`createTimeTravelStoreContext` / `createTimeTravelStore`** | `@context-action/react/time-travel` | Editors, form drafts, and canvas state needing undo/redo history navigation | **Yes (Mutative patches)** | Yes |
| **`createStateStore`** | `@context-action/store-core` | Minimal framework-neutral reference store for Vanilla JS, Node, Preact, Lit, or XState | No | **No (0 deps)** |
| **`createMutativeStateBackend` / `createMutativeTimelineBackend`** | `@context-action/mutative` | Framework-neutral Layer 1 Mutative draft/patch `StateStore` & `TimelineBackend` (`TransactionBackend`), usable standalone or injected natively into React/Lit/Preact | Optional (`TimelineBackend`) | **No** |
| **`createBackendStore` (`BackendStore`)** | `@context-action/react/backend` | Bridge any user-owned `StateBackend` into React subscription hooks (optional when using `createStoreContext().Provider stores={...}`) | Backend-dependent | Yes (wrapper only) |
| **`StoreTransactionCoordinator` + `bindActionTransactions`** | `@context-action/react/transactions` | Group mutations across multiple stores into one atomic commit, rollback, and single undo step | **Yes (atomic multi-store)** | Yes |
| **`useLocalStore` / `useComputedStore` / `StoreRegistry`** | `@context-action/react/advanced` | Component-lifetime local store / memoized derived value / dynamic named store registry | No | Yes |
| **`createRefContext`** | `@context-action/react/refs` | **Non-reactive (Tier 3).** DOM elements, Canvas handles, and 120fps pointer coordinates with zero React re-renders | No | Yes |
| **`createActorStateReader`** | `@context-action/xstate` | **Closed statechart read-only projection.** Blocks external `setValue()`; transitions go through actor events only | No | **No** |
| **`createSourceContext` / `fromStateReader` / `StoreController`** | `@context-action/preact`, `@context-action/lit` | Read-only Signals (`fromStateReader` bridges `StateReader`/`StoreReader` snapshots) or `ReactiveController` projections for Preact/Lit hosts | No | **No** |
| **`createDurableOperationStore`** | `@context-action/tool-durable-operations` | **Not UI state.** Lease/claim idempotency and recovery records for external HTTP, queue, or filesystem side effects | No | **No** |

---

## 2. Store Usage Patterns

### 2.1 `createStoreContext` (`@context-action/react`) — Standard React Domain State

Use `createStoreContext` as the default way to manage domain stores inside a React subtree. It returns `{ Provider, useStore, useStoreManager, useStoreInfo, useStoreClear, withProvider }`.

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```tsx
import { createStoreContext, asStoreValue, useStoreValue } from '@context-action/react';

const {
  Provider: OrderStoreProvider,
  useStore: useOrderStore,
} = createStoreContext('Order', {
  draft: { item: '', qty: 1 },
  // Wrap plain objects that resemble StoreConfig shapes with asStoreValue()
  metadata: asStoreValue({ initialValue: 'custom-user-field' }),
  status: 'idle' as 'idle' | 'submitting' | 'done',
});

// Hook exposing write helper for an Action Handler:
function useOrderQuantityUpdater() {
  const draftStore = useOrderStore('draft');
  return (qty: number) => {
    const current = draftStore.getValue();
    draftStore.setValue({ ...current, qty });
  };
}

// Read inside a View component:
function OrderQuantityBadge() {
  const draftStore = useOrderStore('draft');
  const draft = useStoreValue(draftStore);
  return <span>{draft.qty}</span>;
}

export { OrderStoreProvider, useOrderQuantityUpdater, OrderQuantityBadge };
```

### 2.2 `createStore` (`@context-action/react`) — Standalone Single Store

Use `createStore` when you need a single independent store outside a Provider (module scope, direct prop/DI injection, or focused unit tests). Because `Store` generates Mutative JSON patches, it works directly with `useStorePath`.

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```tsx
import { createStore, useStorePath } from '@context-action/react';

interface ProfileState {
  user: { name: string; age: number };
  theme: 'light' | 'dark';
}

const profileStore = createStore<ProfileState>('profile', {
  user: { name: 'Kim', age: 30 },
  theme: 'dark',
});

profileStore.update((prev) => ({
  ...prev,
  user: { ...prev.user, name: 'Lee' },
}));

export function UserNameLabel() {
  // Re-renders only when ['user', 'name'] is affected by patches
  const name = useStorePath<ProfileState, string>(profileStore, ['user', 'name']);
  return <span>{name}</span>;
}

// Call dispose() when a standalone store's lifecycle ends
profileStore.dispose();
```

### 2.3 `createTimeTravelStoreContext` & `createTimeTravelStore` (`@context-action/react/time-travel`) — Undo / Redo

Use `TimeTravelStore` whenever users need undo, redo, or bounded history navigation.

- `createTimeTravelStore(name, initialValue, { maxHistory, mutable, notificationMode, readMode })` defaults `readMode` to `'reference'` for legacy structural-sharing compatibility.
- Declarative `createTimeTravelStoreContext` defaults `readMode` to `'safe'` and supports symmetric Headless-First DI (`<DocStores.Provider manager={externalManager} />` or `<DocStores.Provider stores={externalStores} ownership="shared" />`) so undo/redo history can live outside React component lifetimes.
- Always read via `store.getSafeValue()` when crossing an external serialization or host boundary.

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```tsx
import { createTimeTravelStoreContext } from '@context-action/react/time-travel';

const DocStores = createTimeTravelStoreContext('Doc', {
  content: { initialValue: { text: '' }, maxHistory: 50 },
});

export function HistoryToolbar() {
  const { canUndo, canRedo, undo, redo, position, historyLength } =
    DocStores.useTimeTravelControls('content');

  return (
    <div>
      <button type="button" disabled={!canUndo} onClick={() => undo()}>Undo</button>
      <button type="button" disabled={!canRedo} onClick={() => redo()}>Redo</button>
      <span>{position} / {historyLength}</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### 2.4 `createStateStore` (`@context-action/store-core`) — Zero-Dependency Reference Store

Use `createStateStore` when you want a lightweight, framework-neutral state container with zero React, Mutative, or DOM dependencies (`capabilities: { patches: false, timeline: false, immutableSnapshots: false }`). The caller owns immutability by passing fresh references; identical `Object.is(prev, next)` updates are skipped.

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```ts
import { createStateStore } from '@context-action/store-core';

const counterStore = createStateStore('counter', { count: 0 });
const unsubscribe = counterStore.subscribe(() => {
  const snapshot = counterStore.getSnapshot(); // { value, name, version, lastUpdate }
  console.log(`v${snapshot.version}: ${snapshot.value.count}`);
});

counterStore.update((prev) => ({ count: prev.count + 1 }));
unsubscribe();
counterStore.dispose?.();
```

### 2.5 `createMutativeStateBackend` / `createMutativeTimelineBackend` & Native Interoperability (`@context-action/mutative` + `@context-action/react`)

Use `createMutativeStateBackend` (`StateStore`) and `createMutativeTimelineBackend` (`TransactionBackend & StateStore`) from `@context-action/mutative` when you want a framework-neutral Layer 1 Mutative engine with JSON patches, undo/redo timeline navigation, and mutable `setNotificationMode('immediate' | 'batched')` shared across React, Lit, Preact, or headless Node workers.

React subscription hooks (`useStoreValue`, `useStoreSelector`, `useStorePath`, `useTimeTravelControls`, `useTimeTravelPath`) and Provider DI (`createStoreContext().Provider stores={...}`, `createTimeTravelStoreContext().Provider stores={...}`) accept `StateReader<T>`, `StateBackend<T>`, and `TimelineBackend<T>` **directly** without requiring manual `BackendStore` boilerplate (while `@context-action/react/backend` `createBackendStore` remains available for explicit standalone wrapping):

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```tsx
import { createStateStore } from '@context-action/store-core';
import { createMutativeTimelineBackend } from '@context-action/mutative';
import { createStoreContext, useStoreValue } from '@context-action/react';
import {
  createTimeTravelStoreContext,
  useTimeTravelControls,
} from '@context-action/react/time-travel';

const sessionBackend = createStateStore('session', { step: 1 });
const docTimeline = createMutativeTimelineBackend('doc', { title: 'v1' }, { maxHistory: 20 });

const SessionStores = createStoreContext('Session', {
  session: { step: 0 },
});
const DocStores = createTimeTravelStoreContext('Doc', {
  doc: { initialValue: { title: '' }, maxHistory: 20 },
});

export function SessionAndDocView() {
  const directStep = useStoreValue(sessionBackend);
  const directTimeline = useTimeTravelControls(docTimeline);
  return (
    <SessionStores.Provider stores={{ session: sessionBackend }} ownership="shared">
      <DocStores.Provider stores={{ doc: docTimeline }} ownership="shared">
        <span>
          Step {directStep.step} (undo={String(directTimeline.canUndo)})
        </span>
      </DocStores.Provider>
    </SessionStores.Provider>
  );
}
```

### 2.5a `createBackendStore` / `BackendStore` (`@context-action/react/backend`) — Explicit Standalone Bridge

Use `createBackendStore` when you want an explicit standalone `IStore` wrapper instance over any `@context-action/store-core` `StateBackend<T, Patch>` (such as `createStateStore`, `MutativeStateBackend`, or a custom persistence/sync backend):

- `ownership: 'shared'` (default): disposing the `BackendStore` wrapper keeps the underlying backend alive.
- `ownership: 'owned'`: disposing the wrapper also disposes the underlying backend.

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```tsx
import { createStateStore } from '@context-action/store-core';
import { createBackendStore } from '@context-action/react/backend';
import { useStoreValue } from '@context-action/react';

const sharedBackend = createStateStore('session', { step: 1 });
const reactStore = createBackendStore('session', sharedBackend, { ownership: 'shared' });

export function SessionStep() {
  const state = useStoreValue(reactStore);
  return <span>Step {state.step}</span>;
}
```

### 2.6 `StoreTransactionCoordinator` & `bindActionTransactions` (`@context-action/react/transactions`) — Multi-Store Transactions

Use `StoreTransactionCoordinator` when a single logical action must update multiple stores without exposing intermediate states and with atomic rollback + single-step undo.

- Participants are registered explicitly (never discovered globally).
- Notifications are deferred until commit flush so readers never observe half-committed pairs.
- For framework-neutral coordination without React, use `bindActionDispatchTransactions` and `runInTransactionScope` from `@context-action/xstate/effect`.

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```ts
import { createTimeTravelStore } from '@context-action/react/time-travel';
import { StoreTransactionCoordinator } from '@context-action/react/transactions';

const cart = createTimeTravelStore('cart', { items: [] as string[] });
const totals = createTimeTravelStore('totals', { price: 0 });
const coordinator = new StoreTransactionCoordinator();

export async function addItemWithRollback() {
  await coordinator.run(
    [
      { name: 'cart', store: cart },
      { name: 'totals', store: totals },
    ],
    () => {
      cart.update((prev) => ({ items: [...prev.items, 'book'] }));
      totals.update((prev) => ({ price: prev.price + 25 }));
    },
    { label: 'addItem' },
  );

  // Undoing the transaction reverts both cart and totals together
  coordinator.undo();
}
```

### 2.7 `useLocalStore`, `useComputedStore`, and `StoreRegistry` (`@context-action/react/advanced`)

- **`useLocalStore(initialValue, name?)`**: creates a component-scoped `Store` and automatically calls `dispose()` on unmount, returning `{ value, name, lastUpdate, store }`.
- **`useComputedStore(store, computeFn, config?)`**: derives and memoizes a computed projection from an upstream store with optional `equalityFn`, `initialValue`, `onError`, and `debounceMs`.
- **`StoreRegistry`**: reserved for advanced dynamic store registration, lookup, and cleanup by string key.

### 2.8 Headless-First Composition (`ActionRegister` DI + `Store` / `StoreManager` / `BackendStore`)

Assemble pure TypeScript orchestration (`ActionRegister`) and state (`createStore`, `StoreManager`, or `@context-action/store-core` `createStateStore`) outside React, then inject both symmetrically into React via `<ActionContext.Provider register={...}>` and `<StoreContext.Provider stores={...} | manager={...}>` (`ownership="shared"` by default):

<!-- @context-action-compile -->
```tsx
import { ActionRegister, type ActionPayloadMap } from '@context-action/core';
import {
  createActionContext,
  createStore,
  createStoreContext,
  useStoreValue,
} from '@context-action/react';

interface CartActions extends ActionPayloadMap {
  addSku: { sku: string };
}

interface CartStores {
  cart: { items: string[] };
}

export const cartStore = createStore<CartStores['cart']>('cart', { items: [] });
export const cartRegister = new ActionRegister<CartActions>({ name: 'HeadlessCart' });

cartRegister.registerCommand('addSku', ({ sku }) => {
  cartStore.update((prev) => ({ items: [...prev.items, sku] }));
});

const CartActionsContext = createActionContext<CartActions>('CartActions');
const CartStoresContext = createStoreContext<CartStores>('CartStores', {
  cart: { items: [] },
});

function CartSummary() {
  const dispatch = CartActionsContext.useActionDispatch();
  const cart = useStoreValue(CartStoresContext.useStore('cart'));
  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => void dispatch('addSku', { sku: 'BOOK-1' })}>
      Items: {cart.items.length}
    </button>
  );
}

export function HeadlessCartView() {
  return (
    <CartActionsContext.Provider register={cartRegister} ownership="shared">
      <CartStoresContext.Provider stores={{ cart: cartStore }} ownership="shared">
        <CartSummary />
      </CartStoresContext.Provider>
    </CartActionsContext.Provider>
  );
}
```

> You can pass `@context-action/store-core` `createStateStore()` or `@context-action/mutative` `createMutativeStateBackend()` directly into `createStoreContext().Provider stores={...}` (`StoreManager` adapts raw `StateBackend` entries automatically) or use `createBackendStore('cart', cartBackend, { ownership: 'shared' })` from `@context-action/react/backend`. For opt-in tree-shaking, specialized React surfaces are also exposed from `@context-action/react/refs`, `@context-action/react/time-travel`, and `@context-action/react/transactions` alongside root `@context-action/react`. For a complete walkthrough connecting specs, intents, and headless DI, see the [Spec-to-Code Authoring Guide](./spec-to-code-authoring-guide.md).

---

## 3. Choosing the Right React Subscription Hook

| Hook | Subscription Granularity | Best Fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`useStoreValue(store, options?)`** | Whole store value (with optional `condition` render gate) | Primitives or small flat objects where most fields render together |
| **`useStoreSelector(store, selector, equalityFn?)`** | Derived slice compared by `equalityFn` | Selecting a single field or computed projection from medium stores |
| **`useStorePath(store, path, options?)`** | Patch-aware path tracking (array segments or RFC 6901 JSON Pointer) | Deeply nested `PatchAwareStore` objects where siblings update independently |
| **`useStoreSelectorWithPaths(store, selector, { dependsOn, equalityFn })`** | Re-runs `selector` only when one of `dependsOn` paths was touched by patches | Expensive multi-field derived selectors over large nested trees |

---

## 4. Non-Store and Cross-Framework Boundaries

Do not force every stateful need into a reactive React `Store`:

1. **`createRefContext` (`@context-action/react/refs`) — Non-Reactive Tier 3 State**: Keep DOM nodes, HTML5 Canvas handles, animation timers, and 120fps pointer coordinates in `createRefContext` so frequent updates never trigger React re-renders.
2. **`createActorStateReader` (`@context-action/xstate`) — Closed Statechart Projection**: Unlike open `StateStore` instances, an XState actor does not allow arbitrary external `setValue()` writes. Route intents through `ActionRegister` / `SyncActionPipeline` (`bindActorToActionRegister` / `bindActorToSyncPipeline`) and read monotonic versioned snapshots via `createActorStateReader(actor, { select, equals })`.
3. **Preact & Lit Read-Only Adapters**:
   - **Preact** (`@context-action/preact`): wrap any `ReadableSource` with `connectSourceSignal(store)` — or adapt snapshot-envelope `StateReader`/`StoreReader` stores explicitly via `fromStateReader(store)` first — and pass it down via `createSourceContext`, projecting slices with `useProjection(signal, selector)`.
   - **Lit** (`@context-action/lit`): attach `new StoreController(this, store, { selector, equalityFn })` to subscribe on `hostConnected()` and clean up automatically on `hostDisconnected()`.
4. **`createDurableOperationStore` (`@context-action/tool-durable-operations`) — Durable Side-Effect Records**: Stores lease/claim status (`pending`, `completed`, `failed`, `unknown`) and reconciliation metadata for external HTTP, queue, or filesystem mutations—it is an idempotency/recovery store, not a UI view store.

# Unified Triad (`ttsc-ex` · `oa-sdk` · `context-action`) Responsibility Split and Self-Serve Sync Guide

**Status:** active  
**Owner:** Framework Core & Architecture Governance  
**Related Docs:** [Implementation Convention](./implementation-convention.md), [CA-SPEC-EVIDENCE-001](./decisions/CA-SPEC-EVIDENCE-001.md), [Convention Index](./convention-index.md), [Panel Layout Preference Convention](./usecase-panel-layout.md)  
**Connected Agent Skills:** [`.agents/skills/context-action-implementation-playbook/SKILL.md`](../../../.agents/skills/context-action-implementation-playbook/SKILL.md), [`skills/context-action-implementation-playbook/SKILL.md`](../../../skills/context-action-implementation-playbook/SKILL.md)

- `ttsc-ex` Unified Hub: `../samchon/docs/cross-repo-responsibility-and-sync-guide.md`

> [!NOTE]
> **Scope — Advisory / Cross-Repo (`ttsc-ex` · `oa-sdk`):** The 3-workspace `.tsp` / `@evidenceReview` contract-lock rules below apply only when working inside a multi-repo Triad setup with companion `../samchon` and `../oa-sdk` checkouts. In `context-action` standalone CI, Step 4 only checks local docs, LLMS sync, and repository conventions (`pnpm docs:management`, `pnpm llms:check`, `pnpm convention:check`).

## 1. Purpose and Three-Workspace Responsibility Boundaries (Zero-Dependency Principle)

Within the Unified Triad architecture, `context-action` owns **frontend modular state management, the action intent pipeline, and viewport layout hierarchy (Pillar 3 & Pillar 4)**.  
Meanwhile, `.tsp` (TypeSpec) domain contract modeling and TypeScript/OpenAPI code generation are owned by **`oa-sdk` (Pillar 1 & 2)**, and requirement anchor verification (`@evidence`) plus compiler graph/hash lock verification (`@evidenceReview`) are owned by **`ttsc-ex` (Pillar 5)**.

This guide explains **how engineers and AI agents working in `context-action` can autonomously read and pull updates from `ttsc-ex` and `oa-sdk` while preserving zero external domain runtime dependencies in `@context-action/core`, `@context-action/react`, `@context-action/preact`, and `@context-action/preact-ui`**.

| Workspace | Core Single Responsibility | Boundary Rule with `context-action` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`context-action`** | • 6-Layer split (`contexts / business / handlers / actions / hooks / views`)<br>• `BusinessActionIntent` vs `LayoutActionIntent` separation (`No Mixed Payloads`)<br>• 3-Tier State Ownership & `Promise.allSettled` parallel aspect hydration<br>• 6-Level layout hierarchy, Two Golden Rules & 4-Tier Semantic Z-Index | `@context-action/*` runtime packages never add direct runtime dependencies on `@typespec/*`, `@oa-sdk/*`, `ttsc`, or `@wrtnlabs/evidence` (**Zero-Dependency preservation**) |
| **`oa-sdk`** | • All `.tsp` domain & governance decorators (`@oa-sdk/typespec-decorators`)<br>• `.tsp` $\rightarrow$ OpenAPI 3.1/3.2 and TypeScript DTO/handler/constant codegen (`oa-gen`)<br>• `x-oa-sdk-trace` + `x-samchon-evidence` JSDoc synthesis | `context-action` applications and examples never parse `.tsp` directly; they consume immutable TypeScript declarations (`dto.ts`, `handlers.ts`, `identity.ts`, `aspect-storage.ts`, `tools.ts`) generated by `oa-sdk` |
| **`ttsc-ex`** | • `@samchon/typespec-evidence` (`@evidence`, `@evidenceExclude`, `## @evidence`)<br>• `ttsc@0.33.1` + `@wrtnlabs/evidence@0.8.0` compiler graph and `@evidenceReview` hash lock gates | Pure functions in `business/` lock generated TS declarations with `@evidenceReview ./generated/dto.ts#... #hash` (or detached `evidenceFiles`) to block spec drift at compile time |
